### Student government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Student government")]

The UAH Student Government Association (SGA) is the primary recipient of student-activity funding from UAH's Office of Student Life. The Space Hardware Club, a registered student organization in the College of Engineering is the secondary recipient. The SGA holds an advisory role with campus administrators on activities involving students. The SGA hosts a number of events including Week of Welcome, an annual event welcoming students back to campus that begins the weekend they arrive on campus and runs through the first week of each fall semester.

### Residence halls

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Residence halls")]

UAH has six residence halls: Central Campus, Charger Village Addition, Charger Village Original, Frank Franz, North Campus, and Southeast. Central Campus, Frank Franz, and North are reserved for first-time freshmen. Frank Franz Hall is reserved for first-time Honors College students. Charger Village Addition and Charger Village Original are reserved for sophomores, whereas juniors and seniors have the option of living at the other residence halls.

Campus housing originated with the construction of Southeast Campus Housing. These suites were originally built under the auspices of the late Dr. Benjamin Graves, the first President of UAH, with the assistance of the late Alabama Senator [John Sparkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sparkman "John Sparkman").

### Greek life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Greek life")]

UAH is home to several [fraternities and sororities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_fraternities_and_sororities "College fraternities and sororities"). Most Greek organizations rent a fraternity or sorority house from the university. Construction of the original houses was made possible by donations from Mark and Linda Smith and Jim and Susie Hudson.

### ACE

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: ACE")]

The Association for Campus Entertainment (ACE) is a student run and operated organization that hosts weekly events throughout the academic year as well as standing programs such as Friday Night Flicks, Sunday Cinema, Late-Night Breakfast, and ACE Wednesday. Notable guests include [Daniel Tosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Tosh "Daniel Tosh") and Recycled Percussion.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Alabama_at_Huntsville#cite_note-31)

### Clubs and organizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Clubs and organizations")]

UAH has more than 150 student-run organizations on campus. Team UAH has won several [concrete canoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete_canoe "Concrete canoe") construction competitions with five national titles in 1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, and 2001. The National Concrete Canoe Competition is sponsored annually by the [American Society of Civil Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Civil_Engineers "American Society of Civil Engineers").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Alabama_at_Huntsville#cite_note-32) The UAH American Society of Mechanical Engineers student chapter also competes in the annual NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge. It holds two championship titles. The UAH Space Hardware Club conceptualizes, designs, builds, tests, and flies hardware for high-altitude balloons, satellites (ChargerSat Program), the CanSat competition, and high-powered rocketry.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Alabama_at_Huntsville#cite_note-33)

### Student Success Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=University_of_Alabama_in_Huntsville&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Student Success Center")]

The Student Success Center (SSC) offers tutoring for nearly all freshman- and sophomore-level courses offered at UAH. Additional tutoring is available for math courses online and in person.

The SSC recruits university students for its PASS (Peer Assisted Study Sessions) program, in which students sit in on courses that they have already succeeded in, and offers class-specific study sessions outside of class, usually 3 hours per week. Historically difficult freshman courses are targeted for PASS, including calculus, chemistry, and economics.
